sources: Ipsos (2018), Perils of Perception – across 19 countries, people guessed that 18–29-year-old women have sex 20 times and men 22 times every four weeks; national surveys put the self-reported figures at about 5 (women) and 6 (men).

Muise, Schimmack & Impett (2016), Sexual frequency predicts greater well-being, but more is not always better, Social Psychological and Personality Science 7(4), 295–302 – 25,000+ Americans (GSS 1989–2012) plus two couple samples; in relationships, well-being rose with sexual frequency up to about once a week, with no further gain beyond; correlational; no link for singles.
